admission.justification: A start-time dependency gate was a real alternative and was rejected for a stated cost; the choice constrains how every master of this repository may be worked.

alternatives.option: Start a leaf without reading its packet's dependencies; the manager orders the landings
alternatives.reason: Parallel starts are the normal flow and a dependency is a landing-order fact, which only the manager holds.

alternatives.option: Refuse a start while a named dependency is unlanded
alternatives.reason: It would serialise a whole master behind its first leaf and turn a landing-order rule into a start error.
alternatives.reconsider_when: a leaf is started whose build cannot be verified without the dependency's landed code, and the parallel start costs a review round.

consequences: The worktree_start description says in one sentence that dependencies are the manager's, and the decision log of a task, not the tool, carries the order.
context: Leaves of one master are started in parallel and synchronised later. A start-time check of the dependencies a packet names would forbid that normal flow, so the packet had to say where landing order lives.
decider: the developer, under D47, as MIK-R83@v1 rule 9 states it
